findings.evidence: template/scripts/pr_review_gate.py:152-165: the `change.parent.name == "archive"` branch resolves `name`, but line 163 still passes `change`, the archived path. openspec_lifecycle.py:679-688 reads `.managed-task.json`, uses `change.parents[2]` as the repo root, and requires `managed_change == change.name`. For `openspec/changes/archive/<date>-<name>` the `payload["change"]` is the canonical name, not the dated directory name, so it exits with 'routing archive gate found invalid managed-task provenance'. `parents[2]` is also `openspec/`, not the repo root. The new tests only use an active change directory, so this is not covered.
findings.summary: handoff_gates calls require_managed_routing_evidence(change) unconditionally, including the archived-change re-admission branch (integration-repair reopen). The design says the gate applies to an active change only. For an archived change the gate looks in the wrong place and refuses, so that supported re-handoff path fails.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_board.py:259 sets `item["handed_off"] = {"head": args.head, "at": utc_now()}`, and the parser (around lines 342-346) has no `--pr`. rehandoff_refusal (lines 308-317) looks the PR up by branch. A closed PR followed by a new PR on the same branch could be matched to the wrong handoff. The artifacts and the code disagree.
findings.summary: The handed-off record stores only head and timestamp. The design and spec say it records the PR (`hand-off --id --head --pr`, `handed_off: {head, pr, at}`). The acceptance check instead re-resolves the PR by branch name via `gh pr view <branch>`.
